item.title: Detecting bus delays and service anomalies in Niterói with autoencoder latent feature representations
item.description: Bus riders judge service by two failures: single trips that run late, and days on which the whole system misbehaves. We ask whether one unsupervised representation of raw GPS telemetry can serve both diagnoses on the NetMob 2026 Niterói bus dataset. An autoencoder compresses each trip into a 64-dimensional latent vector; the frozen encoder feeds supervised delay classifiers, and the reconstruction error serves as an anomaly score. Two findings are negative. First, the latent representation does not improve delay detection: gradient boosting on per-trip summary features reaches $0.846 \pm 0.013 — 来源：arxiv · hackernews — 原文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35710v1

item.title: I built a PyTorch optimizer for large GPU workloads — looking for feedback[P]
item.description: Hey, I've been working on a PyTorch optimizer called ApexW and figured I'd share it here to get some feedback from people who know more about this stuff than I do. The main goal is to reduce optimizer-state memory usage and see how much faster I can make optimizer steps on larger GPU workloads. I've been experimenting with compact optimizer states and a Triton-based execution path. In my current tests, the Triton + compact-state path was around 1.5x faster than PyTorch's fused AdamW on workloads with a few large tensors, and the optimizer-state memory usage was roughly cut in half. item.title: VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
